videoTitle: 7,000+ Reasons The LORD Is Absolutely NOT Tri-Personal

stratagems.name: Extension
stratagems.description: Demands Trinitarianism require plural speech forms (e.g., 'We stretched out the heavens alone') — a criterion no Trinitarian theologian has ever endorsed. Fabricates a falsification condition that the actual position does not imply.

stratagems.name: Equivocation
stratagems.description: Exploits ambiguity of 'alone' (Heb. לְבַדִּי) in Isa 44:24. In context this means without other gods (anti-polytheism polemic), not without intra-divine persons. The entire Isa 44:24 argument collapses if the two senses are distinguished.

stratagems.name: Induction with Concealed Counterexamples
stratagems.description: Claims plural divine references can be 'counted on one hand' while suppressing Gen 1:26, Gen 3:22, Gen 11:7, Isa 6:8, and the divine council Psalms. Pattern repeated from Session 1.

stratagems.name: Pre-loading Advantageous Terms
stratagems.description: Pre-defines the Logos as 'God's literal impersonal speech' before the exegetical question is settled, then reads every NT creation text through this frame without acknowledging the Wisdom/Logos hypostasis tradition.

stratagems.name: Circumstantial Argument / Genetic Fallacy
stratagems.description: Explains why Trinitarians hold their view through historical conditioning rather than engaging the exegetical arguments. Substitutes a causal-psychological account for substantive refutation.

falseClaims.claim: Plural biblical references to God can be 'counted on one hand'
falseClaims.notes: Gen 1:26, Gen 3:22, Gen 11:7, Isa 6:8 are four named examples before consulting the broader divine council Psalms (Ps 82:1; 89:7).

falseClaims.claim: There is no evidence in linguistics that singular pronouns are used to refer to a plurality of persons
falseClaims.notes: GKC §124g documents the pluralis majestatis; Joüon-Muraoka §136d discusses plural of excellence. Both are standard introductory Hebrew grammar textbooks.

falseClaims.claim: Trinitarian use of collective singular necessarily entails partialism
falseClaims.notes: Trinitarian theology holds that singular pronouns apply because three Persons share one undivided divine essence, not because each Person is a part. Partialism is the heresy that each Person is one-third of God — explicitly condemned by classical Trinitarianism.

falseClaims.claim: Dia + genitive in NT creation texts rules out personal agency, indicating only impersonal instrumental causation
falseClaims.notes: Wallace, Greek Grammar Beyond the Basics (pp. 368–369) treats instrumental dia as compatible with personal agents. Heb 1:2 surrounds the construction with highly personal predicates.

falseClaims.claim: NT creation passages are not saying Jesus was a conscious person who created the world with the Father
falseClaims.notes: Col 1:15–20 uses personal pronouns throughout (en autō, autos estin pro pantōn). John 1:1–3 uses pros ton theon (relational personal preposition). The impersonal-word reading requires systematic reinterpretation against the grain of the syntax.

falseClaims.claim: The Messiah was not understood by pre-Christian Jews as a pre-existent spirit being
falseClaims.notes: 1 Enoch 46–48 describes the Son of Man as named before creation; 4 Ezra 12–13 reflects a pre-existent heavenly figure; 11Q13 presents a heavenly redeemer. Pre-existence was not foreign to Second Temple messianic thinking.
